solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Guinea pig fed it in space

indicators.note: fed means given into the mouth, so one word is put inside the other

parts.note: a cavy is the zoological name for a guinea pig
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone feeds their guinea pig with something in an empty space.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavity is a hollow or empty space inside something solid.

clue.text: Small house in weird locale has a cellar

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other
weird means strange, so these letters are put out of order

parts.note: HO is a short form of house

explanation.surface: A small house in a strange location has a cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' scrambles the place name into COALLE; 'in' then slips the short house abbreviation into the middle, between COAL and LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal hole is a small cellar or vault for storing coal.

clue.text: Review managed without English master

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first pair of pieces surrounds the letter

parts.note: to vet is to review or check closely
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Someone checked a review without the English master.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is an old hand, a master of something through long experience.

clue.text: Pastry brought over to character over in restaurant

indicators.note: brought over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tart is a pastry
taken as written

indicators.note: over here means turned round, so this word is read backwards too

parts.note: an air is a character or manner, as in an air of mystery

explanation.surface: A pastry is brought to the person in charge at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' turns TART into TRAT, and 'over' turns AIR into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is a simple Italian restaurant.

clue.text: US marine tossed about on board

indicators.note: being on board means inside, so the short piece goes within the jumbled letters
something tossed about is thrown around, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about or approximately

explanation.surface: An American marine is thrown around on the deck of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed' scrambles the sailor into AMERIN. 'On board' usually means inside SS in crosswords, but here it just means inside the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: American is the adjective for the US, so the abbreviation stands for the word.

clue.text: Dubious activity of male working with important firm

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
key means important, as in a key point
a business is a firm or company

explanation.surface: A man works for a big company doing something shady.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business is an idiom for mischief or underhand dealings.

clue.text: Come to a stretch of open water

definitions.meaning: to arrive at a place or a total
a straight section of a river between bends

explanation.definitionFit: Reach means arrive at, and it is also a straight length of river.

clue.text: Rotter keeping Italian in the Spanish fortress

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a cad is a rotter, a man who behaves badly
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A rotter keeps an Italian locked up in a Spanish fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress, often one guarding a city.

clue.text: React drunkenly after noon drink

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the jumbled letters follow the single letter
drunkenly means unsteadily, so these letters stagger out of order

explanation.surface: Someone reacts drunkenly after a midday drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the drink of the gods, or any delicious drink.

clue.text: Cheeky youngster, one taking picture through

parts.note: to whip is slang for to steal, so one who takes is a whipper
a snap is a photograph
per means through or by means of

explanation.surface: A cheeky young person is caught taking a photo.
explanation.walkthrough: To whip is British slang for to steal, so 'one taking' is a WHIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippersnapper is a young person who is presumptuous or cheeky.

clue.text: A fur almost lost by Asian prince

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: lost means gone astray
a khan is a ruler or prince in Central Asia

explanation.surface: An Asian prince has nearly lost a fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the Y off ASTRAY, leaving ASTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrakhan is the curled fleece of young karakul lambs, used as fur.

clue.text: One with cold is after a dry room

indicators.note: is after means comes later, so the first pair of pieces is placed before the second pair

parts.note: TT, short for teetotal, means dry or not drinking alcohol
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Someone with a cold is looking for a dry room.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is a room in the roof space of a house.

clue.text: Type of car difficult to better

parts.note: difficult means hard
to top something is to better or beat it

explanation.surface: A kind of car that is hard to improve upon.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardtop is a car with a rigid roof, often a removable one.

clue.text: Anteater cruelly chained

indicators.note: cruelly suggests harsh treatment, so these letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: An anteater has been chained up cruelly.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna is the spiny anteater of Australia and New Guinea.

clue.text: Ship emerging from river, on course

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so in an across answer the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a line is a course or direction, as in a line of action

explanation.surface: A ship comes out of a river and heads on its course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emerging from' just links: R comes from river.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship sailing a regular route.

clue.text: Go out with servant, having time off in Welsh town

parts.note: the tide is said to ebb when it goes out

indicators.note: having the letter for time off means that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a valet is a manservant

explanation.surface: A servant gets time off to go out somewhere in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having time off' drops the T of VALET, leaving VALE. EBBW VALE is a town in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebbw Vale is an old steel town in Blaenau Gwent, south Wales.

clue.text: Vault with oven might produce this food item

indicators.note: might produce means could be made from, so the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A baker uses a vault and an oven to make some food.
explanation.definitionFit: A vol-au-vent is a small round case of puff pastry with a savoury filling.

clue.text: Reluctant to go on a river with one old womaniser

parts.note: loth means reluctant or unwilling
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An old womaniser is unwilling to go on a river trip with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, a seducer in an 18th-century play, became a byword for a womaniser.

clue.text: Ranks as a ground state

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so these letters are broken down and rearranged

explanation.surface: Ranks are ground down into a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkansas is a US state in the south, its capital Little Rock.

clue.text: Hors d'oeuvre and portion of bread, sponge later

indicators.note: later means coming afterwards, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a roll is a small portion of bread
to mop is to sponge or wipe up

explanation.surface: Someone eats a starter and then wipes the plate with a piece of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a rolled pickled herring fillet, served as a starter.

clue.text: Extremely tight during card game and bingo

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: loo is an old card game

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Things get very tight while playing cards and bingo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives the two ends of tight; 'during' sets them inside the old card game, which British solvers know from Victorian parlour play.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game like bingo, with numbers drawn and marked off.

clue.text: Milne character, holding his tail, set off

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: Tigger is the bouncy tiger in A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh stories
his here means the Milne character's, and its tail is its final letter

explanation.surface: A character from Winnie-the-Pooh, holding on to his tail, sets off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' points back to the Milne character, so his tail is the last letter of TIGGER, R.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to set it off or start it.

clue.text: The sort of drink to give one courage?

definitions.meaning: a strong alcoholic drink such as whisky or gin
courage or boldness, and also a drink drunk for Dutch courage

explanation.definitionFit: Spirit means a strong distilled drink, and also courage or mettle.

clue.text: Old man describing scented Italian dish

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing a line round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
olent is a rare word meaning fragrant or scented

explanation.surface: An old man is describing a fragrant Italian dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Polenta is an Italian dish of boiled cornmeal.

clue.text: Short statements attack revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: to set on someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A few brief statements are put out to attack a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attack' is the phrasal verb 'set on', and 'revolutionary' reads SETON backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes are brief written statements or memos.

clue.text: Initially, neither of us is hard to feed

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of the next word

parts.note: our means belonging to us
taken as written
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Neither of us finds it hard to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to feed and sustain with food.

clue.text: Right occasion to rotate forward

indicators.note: to rotate means to turn round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an occasion is a time, as in 'that time'

explanation.surface: The right moment arrives to turn something forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to send or pass something on, forward it to another.

clue.text: Commuter's ticket — green, possibly

definitions.note: the definition is commuter, with the 's standing for 'is'

parts.note: a pass is a ticket allowing travel

indicators.note: possibly means maybe in another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A commuter's ticket might be coloured green.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Commuter's' as 'Commuter is'. 'possibly' turns GREEN into ENGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A commuter is a regular passenger on a train or bus.

clue.text: Following videos, attempt needlepoint

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the second piece is placed after the first

parts.note: videos are tapes
to try is to attempt

explanation.surface: After watching videos, someone has a go at needlepoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapestry is decorative needlework, and needlepoint is a form of it.

clue.text: A tape recorder, perhaps, kept in austere office

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the letters lie within the next words

explanation.surface: A tape recorder is kept in a plain office.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereo is a sound system, and a tape recorder is one example.
